reviews.title: Amazing mic for the price!
reviews.comment:
Amazing mic for the price. I’ve had it for one week only and so far loving the result on vocals and electric guitars (Amp).
For now, I will use it mainly for quick recording takes and streaming sessions but I’m starting to think lot’s of these recordings will end up being used.
Sturdy, well-built, light, relatively small and excellent sound. I will leave it on my desk stand constantly and honestly think no $40 dollar mic will get you this far.
Highly recommended!
reviews.author: Sebastian Mejia

reviews.title: High quality sound and build, I bought two
reviews.comment: I bought one initially and was so impressed with the quality, the practically non-existent self-noise, and how my recorded voice sounds, I bought another one. This microphone feels substantial and well-built, very durable. Absolute STEAL at this price point. I'm hoping to use these for stereo recording of chamber music, choirs, etc. I will probably come back and post any recordings I make, especially if they sound as good as I hope they do.
reviews.author: Chancellor Wyman

reviews.title: The $35 Dollar Wonder.
reviews.comment:
It really is a shame Logitech is discontinuing Blue... However, that means you can pick up one of these Embers for dirt cheap now. It's a no-brainer, assuming you have a supporting interface. Mine came with what seems to be the original box and aluminum mount. Condition is so good that I wouldn't be surprised if it was just a brand new one being clearanced as a refurb. I don't know much about the whole situation logistically, but what I do know is that this mic is worth every penny, even at full price.
This mic is excellent for my deep-ish male voice. I run it through a Motu M4, and I sound nearly true to life when I monitor myself, and according to my friends. This is also a wonderful mic for recording acoustic guitar. Very balanced and clear. Just a natural tone all around. You'd be surprised what you can do with it.
Be careful with super cheap mic arms. The Ember was a little heavier than I expected. It's built like a tank. If you get a dirt cheap boom arm, make sure you can lock it in place just in case it struggles to hold the mic up, or just go the extra mile with a better arm.
I'd absolutely buy this again, and will probably pick up a spare. Get them while you can!
reviews.author: Josh M

reviews.title: Almost giving these away...
reviews.comment:
Just purchased my second Ember.  Sturdy, well built metal construction with nice clean sound.  The two I purchased were "Amazon Renewed".  As mentioned by another buyer of an Ember, he purchased the renewed mics as well and described them as like new.  My two arrived in the same like new condition.  No dings or dents... the mic's finish was immaculate.. even the packaging looked new.  The cardboard inner and outer sleeves were perfect.  Highly recommended.
At $40.00 usd is a great deal for this mic.  Don't miss this opportunity.
reviews.author: Xerocoma

reviews.title: Great value XLR microphone
reviews.comment:
I bought the  Blue Ember microphone listed as renewed for $38, and it honestly looks completely brand new. The box still looked factory sealed, had all the original foam padding, manuals, and accessories, and even included a sticker that said “New – Renewed.” on the bottom of the box Based on that alone, it seems like the mic I got  was never  even used.
The mic itself has zero smudges, zero scratches, and no cosmetic damage at all. It looks exactly like a new retail unit. If this is what “renewed” means, I’m more than happy.
Sound quality is excellent for the price. For $38, you’re getting clean, clear audio that works great for vocals, streaming, voiceovers, podcasts, and content creation. Even though Logitech discontinued this mic, it’s still a solid all-around condenser microphone.
At this price, it feels like an absolute steal. If you’re looking for a great-sounding mic on a budget or want to add a versatile mic to your setup, this is a great buy.
